transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Daniel Ortiz (Head of ML, Praxis), Priya Rao (CTO, Praxis), Marcus Lee (Finance, Praxis)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, uh thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Liam our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Daniel: Good, thanks. Thanks for setting this up. We wanted to focus today on cost per token, batching strategies, and what Dedicated or Private would look like for us.
[00:16] Priya: Yeah and I'd add procurement timeline and any SOC2/compliance constraints we need to plan for.
[00:22] Maya: Perfect. Quick agenda — get a sense of your stack and volumes, talk through hosted vs dedicated vs private economics, batching/caching levers, and next steps. Sound ok?
[00:30] Marcus: Sounds good. I'm Marcus, I'll mostly be listening for budget numbers.
[00:34] Liam: Cool, I'll jump in on the performance and batching parts. Daniel, can you start with current usage patterns and models?
[00:40] Daniel: Sure. We're running a hybrid setup today — some internal LLMs on prem for sensitive stuff and a mix of API calls to public providers for client-facing features. Average monthly tokens today around 2 million tokens generated, peak bursts during report runs maybe 400k tokens in an hour. We're planning to ramp to 10M tokens/month over the next 6 months if the pilot goes well. Latency target is sub-400ms for interactive scoring, batch jobs can be higher.
[01:10] Maya: Helpful — and what's the current spend/sensitivity? Any hard budget caps?
[01:15] Marcus: We're looking at a $8k–$12k monthly budget for model inference to start; if economics prove out we can expand.
[01:22] Daniel: Also need to keep data residency in EU for some clients.
[01:26] Liam: Ok, good to know. On Redwood hosted per-token pricing, we have model-specific unit costs — usually cheaper for open-model variants and we expose batching and caching levers to lower effective per-token costs. For Dedicated we provide reserved capacity pricing — flat monthly for a pool sized to your throughput, which can be more predictable at scale. Private adds the overhead of on-prem or VPC deployment and associated licensing.
[01:52] Priya: Can you give examples? Like per-token numbers for a common open Llama-style model vs a larger dense model?
[01:58] Maya: Sure, rough ranges — hosted open models might be in the low single-digit micros per token equivalent, while larger models can be x3–x5. For Dedicated, if you commit to a monthly pool, your effective per-token can drop by 30–60% depending on utilization and batching. We'll send a detailed sheet after the call.
[02:20] Liam: Also important — batching and KV/prefix caching. If your calls are interactive single-turn, you get less batching benefit. But if you can batch 8–16 requests or reuse prompt prefixes we can dramatically drop token/infer cost. For example, for a distributed report generation where prefixes are shared, KV cache can avoid recomputing the same stateless context tokens.
[02:48] Daniel: Wait, quick question — KV cache is server-side caching of key/value attention caches? And that means subsequent tokens are cheaper because the model doesn't recompute?
[02:57] Liam: Yeah, roughly. It's keeping the model's past key/value states so you don't re-encode the same prefix repeatedly. It's most effective for sessions and multi-step flows. The cache reduces compute, so lower cost and lower tail latency.
[03:12] Priya: Any constraints — like does caching change security posture or data residency?
[03:16] Maya: On hosted we have options for caching TTLs and you can opt out for sensitive flows. For Private or Dedicated, caching remains under your control and can be kept inside VPC/on-prem. We'll share our security notes — SOC2, encryption-at-rest and in transit, and KMS integration options.
[03:35] Marcus: About the Dedicated pricing — what are the typical commit sizes and how do overages work?
[03:40] Maya: Typical dedicated pools start around the equivalent of a few A100s or a set of faster inference cards; commit tiers are monthly. Overages are charged at a discounted overage rate; we can model scenarios with your volume.
[03:52] Daniel: For our burst of 400k tokens in an hour, would Hosted handle that or we'd need dedicated?
[03:58] Liam: Hosted can handle bursts — we have autoscaling — but the cost/latency tradeoff differs. For sustained bursts and very tight latency SLOs, Dedicated with reserved capacity gives more predictable latency and lower per-token for high utilization.
[04:12] Priya: And Private on-prem — what's the added cost? Licenses + deployment + ops?
[04:17] Maya: Exactly — Private typically includes platform license, deployment services, and optional support tiers. If you have strict compliance or air-gapped requirements, Private is the route; otherwise Dedicated often hits the balance.
[04:29] Daniel: Marcus jumped in — how do quantization and model variants play in here?
[04:33] Liam: We offer quantized model variants that reduce memory and compute. For example 4-bit or 8-bit quantization can reduce inference cost significantly with small quality tradeoffs on some tasks. We can run per-workload benchmarks.
[04:46] [05:00] Daniel: Ok, can you walk through a simple cost example? Say 10M tokens/month with mix of interactive and batch?
[05:06] Maya: Rough back-of-envelope: hosted open-model per-token cost let's assume $0.000003/token (3 micro). At 10M tokens that's $30. But that's only model compute — real numbers vary by model size, temperature, and effective tokens including prompt length. If you have heavy context and long prompts, costs rise. For a larger model at x5 cost it's $150. With batching and caching you might reduce effective compute by 40% -> so $18–90 ranges. If you go Dedicated, you might be at $0.0000015/token effective which could be $15 on the same volume depending on utilization.
[05:44] Marcus: Those micro numbers seem small — I thought our current vendor charges more.
[05:47] Daniel: Right, current vendor has a more expensive per-token, but they include certain managed features.
[05:52] Liam: The numbers are illustrative — we'll send a detailed spreadsheet that ties model choice, prompt lengths, concurrency, and batching to unit economics.
[06:00] Priya: How much of the savings depends on us changing the app architecture to batch? We don't want to refactor a lot.
[06:06] Liam: If you can accept small batching windows in interactive flows or move heavy work into server-side batch jobs, you can capture most savings. Even minor changes like grouping requests or reusing prefixes can help.
[06:18] Daniel: Another question — can you enforce per-customer quotas and budgets? We need to cap cost per client.
[06:24] Maya: Yes, Redwood Console supports per-token quotas, alerting and cost breakdowns per token and route. You can set hard caps and get alerts when approaching budget.
[06:34] Marcus: For the pilot we mentioned a 100k tokens/month cap, how would that look?
[06:39] Liam: For a 100k pilot, Hosted is simplest — we can set a cap and trace costs. If your pilot shows high utilization we can propose Dedicated sizing.
[06:49] Priya: Security checklist — SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and encryption. Any gotchas?
[06:55] Maya: We support SAML SSO, fine-grained RBAC, audit logs with retention settings, and KMS for key management. For EU data residency we have region-backed hosting and Private deployments. We'll attach SOC2 cert and security whitepaper.
[07:10] Daniel: Perfect. Can the Dedicated or Private options run in our GCP region eu-west-1?
[07:15] Liam: Yes, Dedicated can be provisioned in specific regions. Private is deployed into your VPC or on-prem so you pick the region.
[07:22] Marcus: On the cost modeling workshop — what will you need from us?
[07:26] Liam: Sample prompt set, token length distribution, peak concurrency targets, and any latency SLOs. We'll run synthetic benchmarks and a cost model.
[07:35] Daniel: We can provide that. We'll need assumptions documented so procurement is comfortable.
[07:40] Maya: Great — we'll include assumptions on the spreadsheet.
[07:44] [08:00] Priya: You mentioned KV cache TTLs earlier — what's the typical TTL and privacy implications?
[08:06] Liam: TTLs are configurable. For sensitive data you can set zero TTL (no caching) or short TTLs. On Private/Dedicated caching remains inside your environment so it's compliant with your requirements.
[08:18] Daniel: Any performance numbers on tail latency when using cache vs cold start?
[08:21] Liam: If cache hits are high, tail latency can drop by 20–40% depending on model and sequence length. Cold starts or cache misses will see higher latencies.
[08:32] Marcus: Procurement will ask about SLAs — uptime and latency targets for Dedicated?
[08:36] Maya: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency objectives based on the committed pool and the support tier. We'll include SLA language for review.
[08:46] Daniel: Are there any hidden costs — data egress, logs, long-term storage?
[08:50] Maya: Good callouts. Data egress to/from regions and long-term storage for logs/retention can add costs; we'll document typical billing line items.
[08:59] Priya: For the pilot, what does onboarding look like and timeline?
[09:03] Maya: Onboarding for Hosted pilot is quick — API keys and a couple sample routes in a day or two. For Dedicated sizing/POC, expect 2–6 weeks depending on provisioning. Private on-prem can take longer because of network and install.
[09:17] Daniel: Ok. Can we discuss fallback policies — if Dedicated capacity is saturated, do you auto-failover to hosted?
[09:23] Liam: We support smart routing and fallback policies. You can route by latency/cost/region and have automated fallback to a hosted variant if dedicated capacity is constrained.
[09:33] Marcus: That helps from a continuity standpoint.
[09:37] [10:00] Maya: Quick recap and action items — we'll send the pricing sheet and security docs, Liam will run a sizing workshop and benchmark plan, Praxis will provide prompt sets and volumes, and we'll schedule the SE workshop next week.
[10:13] Daniel: Sounds good. One more nit — do you support per-tenant billing for our internal clients?
[10:18] Maya: Yes, Console has cost breakdowns by route and token key so you can map spend to tenant.
[10:23] Priya: Ok let's wrap — thanks everyone.
[10:27] Marcus: Thanks.
[10:30] [END] Note: transcription has occasional ASR errors and some product names mis-heard (e.g., sometimes "KV cache" rendered as "K V cache"), we left in conversational fillers and overlap for authenticity.
